investigation.name: Demo · real case: Vekselberg's shell companies and the yacht Tango
investigation.question: Through which companies did Viktor Vekselberg own US properties and the yacht Tango, and who kept paying for them after he was sanctioned?
investigation.description: A demo built from three public records: the 2023 S.D.N.Y. civil forfeiture complaint against five US properties, the 2022 D.D.C. seizure-warrant affidavit for the yacht Tango, and OFAC's Federal Register notice of the 6 April 2018 designations. The ownership chains, nominee directors and payments are allegations in the court filings, quoted exactly; the sanctions designation is OFAC's published action. Loaded to show the layered-ownership (BO-002) and shared-address (BO-032) red flags on real data.

claims.rationale: Published by OFAC in the Federal Register.

evidence.quote: 22. VEKSELBERG, Viktor Feliksovich, Russia; DOB 14 Apr 1957; POB Drogobych, Lviv region, Ukraine; Gender Male (individual) [UKRAINE–EO13662].

claims.text: Vekselberg owned the four Medallion properties and the Fisher Island Penthouse through five layers of wholly owned shell companies in Panama, the British Virgin Islands and the Bahamas.
claims.rationale: Alleged in a civil forfeiture complaint; the ownership comes from corporate and bank records the complaint describes.

evidence.quote: Medallion was wholly owned by another Panamanian company (“Company-1”), which, in turn, was wholly owned by a Panamanian foundation (“Foundation-1”).
Foundation-1 was a British Virgin Islands company (“Company-2”), of which Vekselberg was the sole owner.
And in or about 2017, Voxi, which was wholly owned by Medallion, purchased the Fisher Island Penthouse for approximately $31.2 million.

claims.text: Payments for the TANGO were routed through shell companies sharing the same Panamanian nominee directors to hide that Vekselberg owned it.
claims.rationale: The affiant's reading of bank and registry records in a seizure-warrant affidavit.

evidence.quote: Arinter corporate directors Alcides Higuera and Fredis Gonzalez are also officers of Lamesa Transport LLC (“Lamesa Transport”), a Panamanian corporation.
This complicated management and owner structure appears to be for the purpose of obfuscating Vekselberg’s connection to the TANGO
